hero.headline: Woman charged with using vehicle as weapon in St. Lucie County assault
hero.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, sits in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond after authorities charged her with three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. Investigators say Hines used her vehicle to assault three people.

The arrest occurred Saturday in St. Lucie County. Sheriff's deputies took Hines into custody following the incident involving the vehicle.

Hines faces three separate counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. Each count relates to one of the three alleged victims in the case.

A judge set bond at $75,000. Hines remained in St. Lucie County Jail as of Saturday evening.

cards.headline: Indian River County schools develop new strategy to counter enrollment declines amid school choice expansion
cards.body:
Indian River County schools have become the subject of new research examining how the district is working to reverse enrollment declines as school choice options expand across Florida. The case study highlights strategies the district is implementing to retain and attract students in an increasingly competitive educational landscape.

The research comes as school districts across the Treasure Coast face challenges from growing school choice programs that allow families to select from traditional public schools, charter schools, and private schools using state vouchers. Indian River County has experienced enrollment declines as more families exercise these options.

The case study explores specific approaches the district is using to address the enrollment situation. School choice expansion has been a priority of state lawmakers in recent years, giving families more educational alternatives while putting pressure on traditional public school districts to compete for students and the funding that follows them.

The research provides insight into how one Treasure Coast district is adapting to the changing educational environment. Districts rely on per-student funding from the state, making enrollment numbers critical to their budgets and ability to maintain programs and staff.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school sales tax holiday begins July 20, offering 32 days of savings on clothing, supplies and computers
cards.teaser: Florida families can save on essential school items during the state's annual sales tax holiday, running from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026.
cards.body:
Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, running from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day, tax-free shopping period offers significant savings on essential items families need for the new school year, with no sales tax due on qualifying purchases. Tax-free items include clothing such as shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear. Bags including backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs also qualify. Accessories like wallets, belts, ties and graduation caps and gowns are exempt. Notable exclusions are briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100. Tax-free school supplies include pens, pencils, erasers, crayons, notebooks, binders, folders, construction paper, poster board, markers, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes and composition books. Computer disks such as blank CDs only also qualify. Learning materials including flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets are tax-free.

Qualifying computers include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators. Tax-free accessories include keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuner, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use, as business purchases do not qualify. The tax exemption is not available at theme parks and entertainment complexes, hotels and public lodging establishments, or airports. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption, even if delivered after Aug. 20. Price thresholds are $100 per item for clothing and bags, $50 per item for school supplies, $30 per item for learning aids and puzzles, and $1,500 per item for computers and accessories. A family spending $500 on qualifying items could save $35 in sales tax. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

cards.headline: Florida home insurance market shows improvement as insurers return and some rates decline
cards.teaser: Florida's home insurance market is showing signs of improvement with more insurers returning to the state.
cards.body:
The state has seen positive developments in its home insurance market, which has been troubled in recent years. More insurers are returning to Florida and some rates are declining, according to reports. The improvements come after the state has faced challenges with insurers leaving the market due to hurricane risk and rising costs.

The changes represent a shift in a market that has left many homeowners struggling to find affordable coverage. Florida has been working to stabilize its insurance market through various legislative and regulatory measures. The return of insurers and declining rates could provide relief to homeowners who have faced significant increases in recent years.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen selected as FIFA World Cup finals flag bearer
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with news that he will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. Along with the trip, Rosario Liz also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. He explained that the club helped him find his leadership style and redefined his definition of leadership. Rosario Liz said he feels fortunate for everything that has come his way. He closed with a message for the younger members of the club looking up to him, telling them to stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position that he is in right now.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium at the Walton & One development on U.S. 1 and Walton Road, with groundbreaking anticipated for November.
cards.body:
The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028.

The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. Calling it a year-round gathering place, the club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity.

Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements last October when the city was awarded a United Soccer League League One Team. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. The team also said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova beats Coco Gauff in dramatic tiebreaker to reach Wimbledon final
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday in a drama-filled tiebreaker.
hero.body:
Muchova became the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Czech's Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon after wasting five match points
cards.teaser: Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to win Wimbledon on Saturday.
cards.body:
The 21-year-old Noskova overcame Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance. Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club, looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales. Kate presented the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova.

Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Park Vista Cobras football team eyes state playoffs after strong 2025 finish
cards.teaser: Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026.
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find their footing early in 2025 but finished strong by winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the second half of that season felt good, and the team is working toward carrying that performance through a whole season. The Cobras have all the pieces in place now, and it's just about executing, according to Bender. The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Head football coach Donald Hanna emphasized the importance of taking things one game at a time. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs," Hanna said. Senior Erik Lee said the team has the guys needed to get it done but also needs to put the work in to get there. Senior Justice Jones expressed confidence about winning a championship, saying it's going to feel amazing because he already knows it's going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
hero.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes
hero.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, prompting more households to adjust their purchasing decisions based on price rather than preference. For shoppers looking to stretch their dollars, the discount grocer offers an alternative to traditional supermarkets at a time when food costs continue to climb.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "They're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that," she said. The changing shopping habits reflect a broader trend as more households look for ways to manage rising food costs.

Price movements in key grocery categories show a mixed picture for consumers. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Despite some declining categories, the overall trajectory points to continued upward pressure on grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down," they said, adding they would be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase," they said. The new location gives Treasure Coast residents another option for managing household budgets as inflation continues to impact the cost of food.
